An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Notice that we can express the given transformation as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3u+2v-2 \\ 2u+v-1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3u+2v \\ 2u+v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}\end{aligned}
$$

The transformation $T$ maps the boundary of $Δ$ to the boundary of the image. So, to find the image of $Δ,$ we find the images of each side.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14039710/assets/d0103ef8cdf76a3f80bd9be6314c2a693cbf9e51fe66f95228ccce1703f6775f.png)

          

To quickly carry out this calculation, we set up the following matrices:

- The matrix $U$ containing all vertices of our square:

$$
U=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

- The matrix $B$ that has the same shape as $U$ and with the vector $b$ in each column:

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 & -2 & -2 \\ -1 & -1 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

The image of $u$ under $T$ is given by $Au+b.$ So, by applying $T$ to $U,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}AU+B & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 & -2 & -2 \\ -1 & -1 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 3 & 5 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 & -2 & -2 \\ -1 & -1 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & 3 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vertices of the image in the $xy$-plane are $(-2,-1),(1,1),(3,2),$ and $(0,0).$

Drawing this region in the $xy$-plane, we get the following: 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14039710/assets/0b22301fac2a0d97c0f0d99b3c4d162e8965f5570522754a3e21fa124194f1c0.png)

          

Finally, since $det(A)=-1<0,$ this transformation is not orientation-preserving.

An affine transformation T:R2→R2 is a function of the form x=Au+b, where x,u, and b are column vectors in R2, and A is a 2×2 matrix.

Notice that we can express the given transformation as

[xy]=[3u+2v−22u+v−1]=[3u+2v2u+v]+[−2−1]=[3221]⏟A⋅[uv]⏟u+[−2−1]⏟b

The transformation T maps the boundary of Δ to the boundary of the image. So, to find the image of Δ, we find the images of each side.

To quickly carry out this calculation, we set up the following matrices:

  • The matrix U containing all vertices of our square: U=[01100011]
  • The matrix B that has the same shape as U and with the vector b in each column: B=[−2−2−2−2−1−1−1−1]

The image of u under T is given by Au+b. So, by applying T to U, we get

AU+B=[3221][01100011]+[−2−2−2−2−1−1−1−1]=[03520231]+[−2−2−2−2−1−1−1−1]=[−2130−1120].

Therefore, the vertices of the image in the xy-plane are (−2,−1),(1,1),(3,2), and (0,0).
